`IsActionQuotient a π` witnesses that `π : X ⟶ Q` exhibits `Q` as the **quotient of `X` by the
action `a`**: `π` is invariant, and it is *initial among invariant morphisms* — every invariant
`f : X ⟶ Z` factors as `f = π ≫ desc f hf` through a morphism `desc f hf : Q ⟶ Z` that is the unique
factorisation of `f` through `π`.

This is the explicit form of the universal property; see the module docstring for the colimit
interpretation.

Because `π ≫ m` is automatically invariant, `uniq` applies to both maps and forces them equal.

doc:
`tfae_have i → j := t`, where the goal is `TFAE [P₁, P₂, ...]` introduces a hypothesis
`tfae_i_to_j : Pᵢ → Pⱼ` and proof `t` to the local context. Note that `i` and `j` are
natural number literals (beginning at 1) used as indices to specify the propositions
`P₁, P₂, ...` that appear in the goal.

Once sufficient hypotheses have been introduced by `tfae_have`, `tfae_finish` can be used to close
the goal.

All features of `have` are supported by `tfae_have`, including naming, matching,
destructuring, and goal creation.

* `tfae_have i ← j := t` adds a hypothesis in the reverse direction, of type `Pⱼ → Pᵢ`.
* `tfae_have i ↔ j := t` adds a hypothesis in the both directions, of type `Pᵢ ↔ Pⱼ`.
* `tfae_have hij : i → j := t` names the introduced hypothesis `hij` instead of `tfae_i_to_j`.
* `tfae_have i j | p₁ => t₁ | ...` matches on the assumption `p : Pᵢ`.
* `tfae_have ⟨hij, hji⟩ : i ↔ j := t` destructures the bi-implication into `hij : Pᵢ → Pⱼ`
  and `hji : Pⱼ → Pⱼ`.
* `tfae_have i → j := t ?a` creates a new goal for `?a`.

Examples:
```lean4
example (h : P → R) : TFAE [P, Q, R] := by
  tfae_have 1 → 3 := h
  -- The resulting context now includes `tfae_1_to_3 : P → R`.
  sorry
```

```lean4
-- An example of `tfae_have` and `tfae_finish`:
example : TFAE [P, Q, R] := by
  tfae_have 1 → 2 := sorry /- proof of P → Q -/
  tfae_have 2 → 1 := sorry /- proof of Q → P -/
  tfae_have 2 ↔ 3 := sorry /- proof of Q ↔ R -/
  tfae_finish
```

```lean4
-- All features of `have` are supported by `tfae_have`:
example : TFAE [P, Q] := by
  -- assert `tfae_1_to_2 : P → Q`:
  tfae_have 1 → 2 := sorry

  -- assert `hpq : P → Q`:
  tfae_have hpq : 1 → 2 := sorry

  -- match on `p : P` and prove `Q` via `f p`:
  tfae_have 1 → 2
  | p => f p

  -- assert `pq : P → Q`, `qp : Q → P`:
  tfae_have ⟨pq, qp⟩ : 1 ↔ 2 := sorry

  -- assert `h : P → Q`; `?a` is a new goal:
  tfae_have h : 1 → 2 := f ?a

  sorry
```

    let __result ←
      liftM

            let x ← Lean.Meta.mkFreshExprMVar (some (Lean.Expr.sort Lean.Level.zero))
            let x_1 ← Lean.Meta.mkFreshExprMVar (some (Lean.Expr.sort Lean.Level.zero))
            let x_2 ←
              Lean.Meta.mkFreshExprMVar
                  (some
                    ((Lean.Expr.const `List [Lean.Level.zero]).app
                      (Lean.Expr.sort Lean.Level.zero)))
            let matches? ←
              Lean.Meta.withReducible
                  (Lean.Meta.isDefEq
                    ((((Lean.Expr.const `List.cons [Lean.Level.zero]).app
                              (Lean.Expr.sort Lean.Level.zero)).app
                          x).app
                      ((((Lean.Expr.const `List.cons [Lean.Level.zero]).app
                                (Lean.Expr.sort Lean.Level.zero)).app
                            x_1).app
                        x_2))
                    l)
            if matches? = true then do
                let a ← Lean.instantiateMVars x
                let a_1 ← Lean.instantiateMVars x_1
                let a_2 ← Lean.instantiateMVars x_2

    if __result.2.2.2 = true then

        have P' := __result.2.1;
        have l' := __result.2.2.1;

            "unreachable code has been reached"
      else __alt;
  have __alt := do
    let __result ←
      liftM
          (Lean.Meta.withNewMCtxDepth do
            let x ← Lean.Meta.mkFreshExprMVar (some (Lean.Expr.sort Lean.Level.zero))
            let matches? ←

`tfae_finish` closes goals of the form `TFAE [P₁, P₂, ...]` once a sufficient collection
of hypotheses of the form `Pᵢ → Pⱼ` or `Pᵢ ↔ Pⱼ` have been introduced to the local context.

  tfae_have 1 → 2 := sorry /- proof of P → Q -/
  tfae_have 2 → 1 := sorry /- proof of Q → P -/
  tfae_have 2 ↔ 3 := sorry /- proof of Q ↔ R -/
  tfae_finish

doc:
Extract a list of `Prop` expressions from an expression of the form `TFAE [P₁, P₂, ...]` as
long as `[P₁, P₂, ...]` is an explicit list.

signature.text: def Mathlib.Tactic.TFAE.getTFAEList (t : Lean.Expr) : Lean.MetaM (Q(List Prop) × List Q(Prop))

value.text:
fun t => do
  let __do_lift ← Lean.instantiateMVars t
  let __x ← Lean.Meta.whnfR __do_lift
  match __x with
    | tfae.app l => do
      let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.withNewMCtxDepth (Lean.Meta.isDefEq tfae q(List.TFAE))
      have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.MetaM (Q(List Prop) × List Q(Prop)) := fun __r => do
        let __do_lift ← Mathlib.Tactic.TFAE.getTFAEList.getExplicitList✝ l
        pure (l, __do_lift)
      if __do_lift = true then __do_jp ()
        else do
          let __r ←
            Lean.throwError (Lean.toMessageData "goal must be of the form TFAE [P₁, P₂, ...]")
          __do_jp __r
    | x => Lean.throwError (Lean.toMessageData "goal must be of the form TFAE [P₁, P₂, ...]")

doc:
`tfae_have i → j := t`, where the goal is `TFAE [P₁, P₂, ...]` introduces a hypothesis
`tfae_i_to_j : Pᵢ → Pⱼ` and proof `t` to the local context. Note that `i` and `j` are
natural number literals (beginning at 1) used as indices to specify the propositions
`P₁, P₂, ...` that appear in the goal.

Once sufficient hypotheses have been introduced by `tfae_have`, `tfae_finish` can be used to close
the goal.

All features of `have` are supported by `tfae_have`, including naming, matching,
destructuring, and goal creation.

* `tfae_have i ← j := t` adds a hypothesis in the reverse direction, of type `Pⱼ → Pᵢ`.
* `tfae_have i ↔ j := t` adds a hypothesis in the both directions, of type `Pᵢ ↔ Pⱼ`.
* `tfae_have hij : i → j := t` names the introduced hypothesis `hij` instead of `tfae_i_to_j`.
* `tfae_have i j | p₁ => t₁ | ...` matches on the assumption `p : Pᵢ`.
* `tfae_have ⟨hij, hji⟩ : i ↔ j := t` destructures the bi-implication into `hij : Pᵢ → Pⱼ`
  and `hji : Pⱼ → Pⱼ`.
* `tfae_have i → j := t ?a` creates a new goal for `?a`.

Examples:
```lean4
example (h : P → R) : TFAE [P, Q, R] := by
  tfae_have 1 → 3 := h
  -- The resulting context now includes `tfae_1_to_3 : P → R`.
  sorry
```

```lean4
-- An example of `tfae_have` and `tfae_finish`:
example : TFAE [P, Q, R] := by
  tfae_have 1 → 2 := sorry /- proof of P → Q -/
  tfae_have 2 → 1 := sorry /- proof of Q → P -/
  tfae_have 2 ↔ 3 := sorry /- proof of Q ↔ R -/
  tfae_finish
```

```lean4
-- All features of `have` are supported by `tfae_have`:
example : TFAE [P, Q] := by
  -- assert `tfae_1_to_2 : P → Q`:
  tfae_have 1 → 2 := sorry

  -- assert `hpq : P → Q`:
  tfae_have hpq : 1 → 2 := sorry

  -- match on `p : P` and prove `Q` via `f p`:
  tfae_have 1 → 2
  | p => f p

  -- assert `pq : P → Q`, `qp : Q → P`:
  tfae_have ⟨pq, qp⟩ : 1 ↔ 2 := sorry

  -- assert `h : P → Q`; `?a` is a new goal:
  tfae_have h : 1 → 2 := f ?a

  sorry
```
